english.title: Cause death by due care and fail to provide specimen
english.standardoffencewording:
On **(..SPECIFY DATE..) at **(..SPECIFY TOWNSHIP..), caused the death of **(..SPECIFY NAME OF DECEASED AND DATE OF DEATH IF DIFFERENT FROM DATE OF DRIVING..), by driving a mechanically propelled vehicle, being a motor vehicle, namely **(..SPECIFY VEHICLE MAKE AND INDEX NUMBER..), on a

(A)_[road,]_
(B)_[public place,]_

namely **(..SPECIFY ROAD OR PUBLIC PLACE AND LOCATION..), without

(C)_[due care and attention,]_
(D)_[reasonable consideration for other persons using the road,]_
(E)_[reasonable consideration for other persons using the place,]_

and, within 18 hours after that time, were required to provide

(F)_[a specimen or specimens of breath for analysis by means of a device of a type approved by the Secretary of State]_
(G)_[a specimen of blood for a laboratory test]_
(H)_[a specimen of urine for a laboratory test]_

pursuant to section 7 of the Road Traffic Act 1988, but, without reasonable excuse, failed to do so
english.legislation: Contrary to section 3A(1)(c) of the Road Traffic Act 1988 and Schedule 2 to the Road Traffic Offenders Act 1988.
english.pointstoprove:
date and location
caused the death of another by driving a mechanically propelled vehicle
on road/public place without due care and attention/reasonable consideration
within 18 hours were required to provide a specimen for analysis/laboratory test
without reasonable excuse failed to do so

english.notes:
This CJS Code and offence wording is now OBSOLETE - penalty increased - now see CJS Code RT88502 and H6003.

(i) Section 3A(1)(c) only applies in relation to a person driving a motor vehicle (not pedal cycles etc).
(ii) See section 24 of the Road Traffic Offenders Act 1988 for alternative verdicts.
(iii) For the more usual offence wordings relating to the failure to provide specimens see H29 (drive/attempt to drive) and H30 (in charge).
(iv) Officers should ensure they know the C.P.S. guidelines for this offence before preparing any charges. When investigating these offences consideration must be given to the advice offered in the charging standards. See the general guidelines and the specific guidance for causing death whilst under the influence.

other.penalty:
Ten years imprisonment and / or a fine.

Obligatory disqualification and endorsement.

Obligatory endorsement - licence endorsed three to eleven penalty points - only if special reasons apply.

Time limit for prosecutions:
None
